name: ch.antevo/trademark
title: Antevo Trademark
description: Screen a name in 50+ trademark registers (Swiss, EU, UK, US), company and domain checks. No account.

tools.name: screen_mark
tools.description:
Screens one brand name against trademark registers. No account needed.

    Returns the registered and pending marks closest to the name (up to 25), each with a
    similarity tier, and the registers those marks are filed in. EU marks come from
    EUIPO's search; the other registers are read from Antevo's copy, refreshed from each
    office, so a filing from the last few days can be missing. It is a screen, not
    clearance.

tools.name: check_names
tools.description:
Screens a shortlist of up to 15 candidate names in one call: the trademarks on
    file near each name, the companies registered under it, and whether its domains are
    registered. Ranks them fewest conflicts first: by how close the nearest mark is, then
    by companies registered under the name and domains taken, then by how many near marks
    there are. No account needed.

    Optional `classes` (Nice class numbers) make marks filed only in unrelated classes
    weigh less; without them, a mark in any class counts. The Swiss company register and
    the .ch and .com domains are always checked; `countries` ("UK", "SG") adds those
    company registers, and .sg for Singapore.

    Returns, for each name, a trademark verdict on what is on file (none_found, similar,
    close or identical), how many near marks were found, where they are filed and the
    closest three; per country, the companies registered under the same or a similar
    name (name and legal form only); and whether each domain is registered or appears
    unregistered. A source that did not answer says not_checked, never that nothing is
    on file, and names whose trademark screen did not finish are listed under
    not_checked. none_found means none were found, not that the name is free to use, and
    an unregistered domain can be taken at any time: it is a screen, not clearance, and
    a filing from the last few days can be missing.

tools.name: suggest_classes
tools.description:
Which Nice classes a business like this files in. No account needed, and no
    register is searched: it maps the description onto the Nice classification.

    The question people cannot answer for themselves: not "is my name taken" but
    "taken in WHAT". Nice has 45 classes and the numbering is opaque — software you
    download is class 9, software you log into is class 42, and selling other people's
    goods is class 35 whatever the goods are. Filing in one and not the other is the
    most expensive routine mistake in the process.

    Takes a description of the business and returns the classes similar businesses
    file in, with the reasoning for each and a closing caveat: this reports how
    similar businesses file, not what this one should file.

tools.name: holder_read
tools.description:
Who a holder is and how they file — the read on an adversary. Free.

    Computed from their whole register book: how much of it they let lapse, whether
    their marks cluster where they trade or spray across unrelated classes, and the
    leverage that gives counsel. Returns the evidence behind each finding; it draws no
    legal conclusions about the holder. Corporate identity from PermID comes with
    `attribution`, its CC BY 4.0 credit.

tools.name: opposition_window
tools.description:
How long you have to oppose a filing in a given trademark office, and from when.

    Twenty registers, each with the provision the window comes from. The trap this
    answers: most offices run opposition BEFORE registration, from publication of the
    application, but a minority — Switzerland, Germany, Japan, Sweden — register the
    mark first and run the window from publication of the REGISTRATION. Applying one
    office's rule to another invents a deadline that never existed.

    Accepts a country name, an office name or a two-letter code ('japan', 'JP', 'EU').

tools.name: filing_landscape
tools.description:
Filing activity in a Nice class — volume by month and the busiest filers. Signed-in.

    Answers "how crowded is my space" and "who keeps filing near me". Pass a Nice
    class (9, 42, 36…), optionally an office code ('EM', 'US', 'GB', 'CH'), and a
    window in months.

    EVERY COUNT IS OF OUR MIRROR, NOT OF THE OFFICE, and the two differ by a lot for
    some offices right now. Each office carries its own `coverage`, and any office
    whose mirror is behind is named in `do_not_quote`: for those offices a low count
    means filings not yet ingested, not filings that were never made.

tools.name: my_conflicts
tools.description: Everything currently near the names this user watches.

tools.name: my_deadlines
my_watches
tools.description: The names this user is watching.

tools.name: company_file
tools.description:
A holder's WHOLE book across every office. Founder and up.

    Corporate identity from PermID (organisation, HQ, PermID) comes with
    `company.attribution`, its CC BY 4.0 credit.

tools.name: follow_filer
tools.description:
Follow an adversary — every filing they make, anywhere. Studio and up.

    Different from watching a name: this catches what they do NEXT, which is usually
    a different name in a class the user doesn't hold.

tools.name: watch_mark
tools.description:
Start watching a brand name: new filings near it show up as conflicts.

    Optionally takes Nice classes as a comma-separated list ('9,42'); blank watches
    every class.

tools.name: dismiss_conflict
tools.description:
Clear one hit as not-a-threat. Reversible — it moves to the Cleared list.

    Takes `jurisdiction` and `app_no` exactly as they appear on a conflict in the
    user's conflict list. A cleared hit, such as an unrelated business or the user's
    own filing, stops being surfaced.

tools.name: filer_activity
tools.description: What the filers this user follows have filed lately. Studio and up.

tools.name: run_investigation
tools.description:
Research a trademark holder on the open web and return a cited dossier: who they
    really are (an operating company, a shell, a known squatter), their notable
    trademark activity or disputes, and any red flags. Signed-in.

    Spends one credit — included credits first, then purchased ones. A failed run
    costs nothing, and calling again for the same holder within 30 minutes returns that
    dossier at no charge (`reused: true`). The dossier is AI-written from cited web
    sources: research to check, not register fact.

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.description:
How many credits this user can spend and what each paid tool costs, in credits.
    Free to call.

    `remaining` is what can be spent now: `monthly_left` (included with their plan,
    resets each month) plus `topup_balance` (bought, never expires). `prices` is
    credits per call, by tool.
